insights.insight: Crinkl crossed $2M in cryptographically verified cumulative GMV on 2026-06-14, with a full-snapshot figure of $2.42M including the alpha base — confirming the protocol is processing real consumer spend at scale, not pilot volume.

The protocol is ingesting approximately 420 receipts per day, with 34,518 cumulative receipts confirmed — a cadence that generates statistically meaningful purchase signals across grocery, dining, retail, and home improvement without relying on probabilistic inference.

Walmart (323 receipts), Costco (151), Home Depot (84), and Kroger (69) lead the 14-day brand count, with grocery and restaurants each clearing 1,100+ receipts — the coverage map already reflects the categories where most CPG and retail brand budgets compete.

The 7-day average basket has rebounded to ~$80.40 after a prior compression period that pushed averages into the $58–60 range; the 14-day named-category average still runs ~$57, so the recovery is real but narrow and warrants watching across a longer window before treating it as a trend reversal.

189 receipts in an uncategorized bucket carry a $354 average basket in the 14-day window — roughly 6x the named-category average — suggesting large-ticket digital or B2B spend is entering the verified stream and may represent a distinct high-value targeting segment once resolved.

YouTube receipts are appearing in brand-level data, confirming the protocol's DKIM-verified allowlist now reaches digital subscription purchases alongside physical retail — expanding the addressable signal set for marketers targeting streaming and software audiences.
